key_insight: For geometry-aware hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and physics-based constraints work best during fine-tuning, while out-of-distribution performance is primarily limited by geometric coverage.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable prediction of patient-specific aortic velocity and pressure fields toward real-time cardiovascular assessment.
method: Generate synthetic aortic CFD solutions with automatically adjusted boundary conditions for physiological consistency.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields from a common reference and train Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net models at peak systole.
Evaluate active-learning acquisition strategies and differentiable finite-element residual constraints.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on the SynthAorta-based CFD dataset show little early-training benefit from active learning, but gains from gradient- and subspace-based acquisition during fine-tuning; physical constraints are also more effective during fine-tuning.
watch_item: Generalization to unseen anatomies remains constrained by the geometric support of the underlying parametrization.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
